$comment: What each surface of each corpus currently measures, written by scripts/surface-leakage-gate.py --sync and enforced by the same script with no argument. `separability` is max(auc, 1-auc) for a naive-Bayes classifier predicting accept-or-reject from that surface alone, under stratified cross-validation averaged over a fixed seed list; 0.5 is chance. A figure above its recorded value refuses, whether or not the surface is already over target. A figure over `target` refuses unless the row names the constraint blocking it, and a row that names one after coming back under target refuses as a stale declaration. Do not raise a number here to quiet the gate: the recorded figure is the level a surface has reached and the only sanctioned way to move it up is to have a reason a reader accepts.

identifier.blockedBy: the published identifier namespace, filename and directory both
identifier.reason: Measured over the vector's whole manifest-relative path, this surface is a PERFECT predictor: the `ok-`/`bad-` prefix and the `accept/`/`reject/` directory each name the label outright, and either alone is enough. The figure was recorded lower before the surface was widened from the filename to the path, which understated it -- a content-addressed filename left inside `accept/` would have moved the leak rather than removed it and this gate would have gone green on the way past. The fix is to content-address the identifier and flatten the corpus into one directory, retiring every old identifier permanently; GOVERNANCE.md's commitment is that an identifier is never REUSED, which a permanent retirement honours. It is in progress and this row records the level it starts from.

lexicon.blockedBy: a second attack class carried more often on the accept side
lexicon.reason: The margin over target is a hundredth and it is one regularity: statements naming a second attack class in the corpus manifest sit more often on the accept side, because the vectors built to exercise multi-class coverage are mostly conformant ones. Closing it means adding reject vectors over the same shape rather than removing anything.

all.blockedBy: the published identifier namespace, filename and directory both
all.reason: Carried by the identifier surface above and by almost nothing else.

file.blockedBy: one template supplying most of the accept side
file.reason: The accept side carries `predicate.contentDigest` on most of its members and the reject side on almost none, because the RFC 8785 Appendix B number-serialization family is entirely on the accept side and has no reject counterpart. The presence of one member path therefore very nearly names the label, and it is why de-leaking the identifier alone does not bring this corpus near target. The fix is on the reject side: Appendix B rows that serialize the number wrongly, built from the same template.

all.reason: Both causes at once. Unlike the other corpus this one leaks through its content on its own, so the identifier fix does not take it to chance.
